Black powder does not fully combust and spews a lot of unburned powder around. In a closed-to-fire action gun like a bolt or lever-action, most of that goes out the end of the barrel in the direction of the bullet. In a black powder revolver that blows out between the cylinder/barrel gap. In these guns this gap is wider than in smokeless powder revolver to prevent seizing up. In a gun that uses the bolt opening to cycle (like an SMG or semi-auto) unburned powder will dump directly into the moving bits and jam the gun.
